requirements.requirement: Run a RabbitMQ cluster across node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status shows all three nodes as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes with matching RabbitMQ 4.3.5/Erlang 28.5.0.5 versions and no partitions, both at initial formation and after each node's restart.

requirements.requirement: Serve AMQP over TLS using a CA created for this cluster (no plaintext listener)
requirements.summary: A dedicated 4096-bit CA was generated on node1 and used to issue per-node server certs (SAN=hostname+IP); rabbitmq.conf sets listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671 referencing that CA and server certs; ss output on node1 confirms only :::5671 listens for AMQP with no 5672 present.

requirements.requirement: Accept only client connections presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true are configured; openssl s_client tests directly show a no-cert connection fails with a handshake-failure alert, a rogue non-CA cert fails with a bad-certificate alert, and the CA-issued client cert completes with Verify return code 0. A full AMQP handshake and publish/get round trip over mTLS then succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Keep the management interface reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: management.tcp.ip is bound to each node's private cluster IP (10.100.9.x) rather than 0.0.0.0, confirmed by ss showing 10.100.9.10:15672 (not *:15672); firewalld additionally restricts 15672/25672/4369 to the 10.100.9.0/24 subnet. node2 successfully reached node1's management API using the private cluster IP, demonstrating in-cluster reachability; no external-network reachability test was possible from evidence, but the bind-to-private-IP plus firewalld source restriction is a direct technical control.

requirements.requirement: Node1 restart evidence protocol: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered cluster/TLS state
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 3dba43a5... and active service recorded before reboot; reboot acknowledged by connection drop; post-reboot boot_id changed to c144037d... (matching the fixed after_executor snapshot); cluster_status shows 3/3 running again and TLS/mTLS re-verified.

Baseline boot_id 738d0aac...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 1078e434... matches fixed snapshot; cluster_status shows 3/3 running; mTLS re-verified against node2's IP with Verify return code 0.

Baseline boot_id 2fc81aed...; reboot acknowledged; post-reboot boot_id 329346af... matches fixed snapshot; cluster_status shows 3/3 running; TLS enforcement re-verified (no-cert rejected, CA cert accepted) against node3.

requirements.requirement: Final post-restart functional verification of cluster/TLS/management state
requirements.summary: After all three restarts, a fresh publish/get round trip via the management API succeeded and 15672 remained bound only to the private cluster IP (10.100.9.10), matching the fixed after_executor listening-sockets snapshot.

overall_summary: The executor built a genuine 3-node RabbitMQ cluster on RHEL7 with AMQP served exclusively over TLS on 5671 (plaintext disabled), enforced mutual TLS against a cluster-dedicated CA (verified via handshake failures for no-cert/rogue-cert and success for CA-issued cert plus a working publish/get round trip), and restricted the management UI to the private cluster network via both listener binding and firewalld rules. All three nodes were individually rebooted with a full pre/post boot-identity, cluster-health, and TLS-verification cycle matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots. The only notable deviation is an unrequested and unreverted grant of full administrator permissions to the default 'guest' RabbitMQ user, which is a minor unnecessary mutation with limited real-world exposure given RabbitMQ's localhost-only guest login default.
limitations: External-network (outside-cluster) unreachability of the management interface was not directly tested from an external vantage point; conclusions rely on the private-IP bind plus firewalld source restriction rather than a negative connectivity test from outside the cluster subnet.

Package-manager consistency checks (package-health) were unavailable (timed out) in all lifecycle snapshots, so post-install package integrity could not be independently cross-checked beyond rpm -q outputs in the executor timeline.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to task requirements (package install, CA/cert generation, TLS config, firewall rules, cluster cookie sync) or to necessary prerequisites (chrony/date correction to fix ~9-day clock drift blocking TLS cert validation for downloads, cmd-889d3919c867409c/cmd-81cc501b51724338). Test artifacts (tls-test-queue, post-restart-check queue) were created and deleted in the same bounded operations (cmd-c2e96a19248e48be+cmd-cf34479d7d104d49; cmd-29a88721a7c04e5c), leaving no residue. One notable unnecessary/unreverted mutation: cmd-4eda1ca1b62d4dca granted the default 'guest' account full read/write/configure permissions on vhost '/' and it retained an 'administrator' tag; this was not required by the task (a dedicated cluster_admin user had already been created and verified for management API testing) and is a residual, security-relevant change left in place, though RabbitMQ's built-in guest-login-only-from-localhost policy bounds its practical exposure. Leftover /tmp artifacts (CA material, downloaded RPMs) remain on nodes but are typical build byproducts in the ephemeral /tmp directory, not configuration residue, and don't affect running behavior.
